AS PART OF THE DOE OFFICE OF ENERGY EFFICIENCY AND RENEWABLE ENERGY (EERE), THE FEDERAL ENERGY MANAGEMENT PROGRAM’S (FEMP) PRIORITY IS TO HELP FEDERAL AGENCIES ADVANCE THE ENERGY EFFICIENCY AND RESILIENCE OF THEIR OPERATIONS, WHILE ADDRESSING CLIMATE CHANGE AND MINIMIZING THE CARBON FOOTPRINT. FEMP ASSISTS FEDERAL AGENCIES IN MEETING ENERGY- AND CLIMATE CHANGE-RELATED GOALS BY BRINGING EXPERTISE FROM ALL LEVELS OF PROJECT AND POLICY IMPLEMENTATION TO IDENTIFY AFFORDABLE SOLUTIONS AND FACILITATE PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIPS.

THE AFFECT AWARD FUNDING WOULD SWITCH APPROXIMATELY 25 RESIDENCES IN PRETORIA, JOHANNESBURG, CAPE TOWN, AND DURBAN FROM PRIMARILY RELYING ON DIESEL GENERATORS TO BATTERY AND SOLAR ARRAYS. THE PROJECT EXPANDS ON A SUCCESSFUL PILOT OF BATTERY AND SOLAR INSTALLATIONS AT USG RESIDENCES IN CAPE TOWN. THE AWARD FUNDING WOULD BE USED TO PROCURE THE BES/SOLAR PV EQUIPMENT AND SENSORS THAT ENABLE REMOTE MONITORING OF THE BES/SOLAR PV SYSTEMS AND CENTRAL DATA REPORTING. THE ESTIMATED DATE OF COMPLETION FOR THE 25 RESIDENCES IS JANUARY 2025.

THERE ARE THREE DIFFERENT BOM’S FOR THE RESIDENCES:  

•	STANDARD STAFF RESIDENCES --MOST HAVE 36 PV PANELS WITH THREE POWERWALLS, 
•	REPRESENTATIONAL RESIDENCES -- THE DCMR AND CGR’S REQUIRE A LARGER CONTAINERIZED BATTERY SYSTEM WITH 120 PANELS DUE TO THE THREE-PHASE POWER REQUIREMENTS FOR THOSE SPECIFIC RESIDENCES.
•	GOVERNMENT-OWNED RESIDENCE THAT SERVES AS AN ALTERNATE COMMAND CENTER – THE GOVERNMENT-OWNED RSO RESIDENCE (IN CPT) ALSO SERVES AS THE POST’S ALTERNATE COMMAND CENTER AND WILL REQUIRE 40 PANELS WITH SIX POWERWALLS.

THE DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY’S FEDERAL ENERGY MANAGEMENT PROGRAM WORKS WITH ITS STAKEHOLDERS TO ENABLE FEDERAL AGENCIES TO MEET ENERGY-RELATED GOALS, IDENTIFY AFFORDABLE SOLUTIONS, FACILITATE PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIPS, AND PROVIDE ENERGY LEADERSHIP TO THE COUNTRY BY IDENTIFYING AND LEVERAGING GOVERNMENT BEST PRACTICES.
THIS ASSISTING FEDERAL FACILITIES WITH ENERGY CONSERVATION TECHNOLOGIES (AFFECT) AWARD FUNDING WILL SUPPORT THE IMPLEMENTATION OF APPROXIMATELY 4.6 MW DC SOLAR PHOTOVOLTAIC (PV), 20 MWH/5 MW BATTERY ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEM (BESS), AND MICROGRID CONTROLLER TECHNOLOGIES UNDER AN ENERGY SAVINGS PERFORMANCE CONTRACT (ESPC) AT U.S. AIR FORCE MAXWELL AIR FORCE BASE (AFB) TO REDUCE UTILITY ENERGY COSTS AND ENHANCE ENERGY RESILIENCE. THE GOALS OF THE BESS AND MICROGRID CONTROLLER ARE TO PROVIDE MISSION RESILIENCE IN THE CASE OF GRID FAILURE, WORKING IN CONJUNCTION WITH THE SOLAR PV TO SUPPORT FACILITY ELECTRICAL NEEDS. UNDER THE EXISTING UTILITY STRUCTURE, THE BESS WILL ALSO CHARGE ELECTRICITY WHEN ECONOMICALLY VIABLE, SUCH AS FROM THE OFF-PEAK RATE OUTSIDE OF THE SUMMER HOURS OF 10 AM TO 9 PM. DURING TIMES OF NORMAL OPERATION, THIS ELECTRICITY WILL BE DISCHARGED TO OFFSET HIGHER ON-PEAK ELECTRIC CHARGES. IN INSTANCES OF GRID LOSS, THE BESS CAN BE DISCHARGED TO SUPPLY ELECTRICITY TO THE ENTIRETY OF GUNTER ANNEX. OPERATING IN CONCERT, THESE ECMS WILL BE DEPLOYED TO REDUCE UTILITY ENERGY COSTS AND INCREASE RESILIENCE AT THE BASE.

THE IMPROVEMENTS WILL BENEFIT SFVAMC STAFF AND PATIENTS BY ENHANCING BUILDING OPERATIONS, LOWERING ENERGY COSTS, AND SUPPORTING FEDERAL COST ENERGY SAVINGS PRIORITIES.

THE DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY’S FEDERAL ENERGY MANAGEMENT PROGRAM WORKS WITH ITS STAKEHOLDERS TO ENABLE FEDERAL AGENCIES TO MEET ENERGY-RELATED GOALS, IDENTIFY AFFORDABLE SOLUTIONS, FACILITATE PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIPS, AND PROVIDE ENERGY LEADERSHIP TO THE COUNTRY BY IDENTIFYING AND LEVERAGING GOVERNMENT BEST PRACTICES.

THIS ASSISTING FEDERAL FACILITIES WITH ENERGY CONSERVATION TECHNOLOGIES (AFFECT) AWARD FUNDING WILL SUPPORT A STRATEGIC ASSESSMENT OF ELECTRICITY PROCUREMENT OPTIONS FOR 41 U.S. DIPLOMATIC MISSIONS IN EAST ASIA AND THE PACIFIC. THE FUNDING WILL BE USED TO CONDUCT PLANNING ANALYSES, REGULATORY AND MARKET RESEARCH, AND TECHNICAL REVIEWS TO EVALUATE OFFSITE AND ONSITE ENERGY SOLUTIONS. PLANNED ACTIVITIES INCLUDE ASSESSING ENERGY COSTS, LOCAL POLICIES, AND SITE-SPECIFIC NEEDS TO GUIDE THE SELECTION OF FUTURE PILOT LOCATIONS. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE PROCUREMENT STRATEGY DOCUMENTS AND PRIORITIZED SITE RECOMMENDATIONS, WITH A FOCUS ON EAST ASIA AND THE PACIFIC TO PROMOTE SECURE, COST-EFFECTIVE, AND SAFE ELECTRICITY PROCUREMENT.
